facts.value: City of Alachua, Florida; proposed Ordinance 26-17 concerning a temporary moratorium on data center development applications.
facts.supporting_quote: Ordinance 26-17 - AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COMMISSION FOR THE CITY OF ALACHUA, FLORIDA, IMPOSING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM

facts.value: The September 14 minutes report a 5-0 roll-call vote on Vice Mayor Ringersen's motion to establish a temporary twelve-month moratorium and have staff draft an implementing ordinance.
facts.supporting_quote: Vice Mayor Ringersen moved to establish 1) a temporary twelve-month moratorium ... 2) that staff draft an ordinance to implement a temporary moratorium ... Passed 5-0 by roll call.

facts.value: Commissioner Fletcher's separate motion concerning review and possible deferral of data-center-related comprehensive plan amendments died for lack of a second.
facts.supporting_quote: Mayor Welch announced that the motion died for lack of a second.

facts.value: For October 5, staff recommended first-reading approval and scheduling second and final reading for October 26.
facts.supporting_quote: the ordinance as presented be approved on first reading and ... second and final reading be scheduled for October 26, 2026.

facts.value: The unsigned October 5 minutes report that a motion to pass Ordinance 26-17 on first reading and schedule final reading for October 12 passed 4-1, with Commissioner Youmas dissenting.
facts.supporting_quote: pass Ordinance 26-17 upon first reading and ... schedule second and final reading for October 12, 2026 ... Passed 4-1 by roll call, with Commissioner Youmas dissenting.

facts.value: A later motion sought changes to section 7, a medium-data-center definition and a special study group. An amendment removing the medium-data-center language and the underlying motion each failed 2-3, with Welch, Ringersen and Brown dissenting.
facts.supporting_quote: Amended Motion failed 2-3 by roll call ... Motion failed 2-3 by roll call

facts.value: Resolution 26-17 was a separate item in the budget hearing, not the data center moratorium ordinance. The minutes report that resolution passed 3-2.
facts.supporting_quote: Vice Mayor Ringersen moved to adopt Resolution 26-17 ... Passed 3-2 ... Vice Mayor Ringersen moved to adjourn the budget hearing ... B) ORDINANCE 26-17

facts.value: The October 26 agenda item reports that Ordinance 26-17 passed first reading on October 5 and recommends passage and adoption on second and final reading.
facts.supporting_quote: Staff recommends that City Commission pass and adopt Ordinance 26-17 upon second and final reading. ... On October 5, 2026, the City Commission passed Ordinance 26-17 upon first reading.

facts.value: The draft would prohibit the city from accepting, processing, reviewing, scheduling for hearing or approving development applications for construction, establishment, location, expansion or change of use to a data center facility within city limits.
facts.supporting_quote: shall not accept, process, review, schedule for hearing, or approve any Development Application for the construction, establishment, location, expansion, or change of use to a Data Center Facility

facts.value: The draft definition includes data centers, large-scale data centers, certain large-load-customer facilities principally used for data processing, storage or transmission, and cryptocurrency mining operations with their supporting infrastructure.
facts.supporting_quote: any Data Center, Large-Scale Data Center, facility of a Large Load Customer whose principal use is data processing, storage, or transmission, or Cryptocurrency Mining Operation

facts.value: The draft provides exemptions for qualifying accessory computer uses, certain existing lawful facilities, governmental and public safety facilities, specified telecommunications and utility facilities, and hurricane repair required by applicable law.
facts.supporting_quote: This Ordinance does not apply to: ... Accessory computer uses ... Existing lawful facilities ... Governmental and public safety facilities ... Telecommunications and utilities ... Hurricane Repair.

facts.value: The draft term is twelve months from its effective date or until relevant comprehensive-plan and land-development amendments become effective, whichever is first. One extension of up to six months by ordinance is permitted under specified conditions, and early termination by ordinance is allowed.
facts.supporting_quote: twelve (12) months from the effective date ... or until the effective date of ordinance(s) adopting ... amendments ... whichever occurs first. ... The Commission may extend the moratorium one time, for a period not to exceed six (6) months

facts.value: The draft directs the city manager, through planning staff and in coordination with the city attorney, to present findings and recommended regulatory amendments no later than nine months after the ordinance's effective date.
facts.supporting_quote: shall present findings and recommended amendments ... no later than nine (9) months after the effective date of this Ordinance.

facts.value: The draft provides that the ordinance would become effective upon passage and adoption on second and final reading.
facts.supporting_quote: This Ordinance shall be effective upon its passage and adoption on the second and final reading.

facts.value: The October 26 packet contains an unsigned ordinance signature page preprinted with an October 26 second-reading adoption date; it is not by itself evidence of completed adoption.
facts.supporting_quote: Staff recommends that City Commission pass and adopt Ordinance 26-17 upon second and final reading. ... upon second reading this 26th day of October, 2026.
